lesson.child_mission: Creating a presentation organises the inquiry story: question, sources, findings, conclusion, credits and thanks. Visuals support evidence; they do not replace it.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
List five sections every inquiry presentation should include.

FEEDBACK
Question; findings/evidence; conclusion; sources; (and typically method or limits) — accept clear five.

WATCH FOR
Decorative slides with no sources fail the history purpose.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Build presentation cards/slides with a visible source list. Script 2–3 minutes. Include respect credit for any First Nations content.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Build presentation cards/slides with a visible source list. Script 2–3 minutes. Include respect credit for any First Nations content. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using presentation on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: Decorative slides with no sources fail the history purpose.. Correction: Question; findings/evidence; conclusion; sources; (and typically method or limits) — accept clear five.. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: Decorative slides with no sources fail the history purpose. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating presentation on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with presentation, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about presentation with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for presentation. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example slide/card order: question → map/timeline → three findings → conclusion → source list → Acknowledgement if appropriate to school protocol.

TRY FIRST
List five sections every inquiry presentation should include.

FEEDBACK

teach_steps.explain:
Creating a presentation organises the inquiry story: question, sources, findings, conclusion, credits and thanks. Visuals support evidence; they do not replace it.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the sources, map features or community examples that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a detail is uncertain, identify what source you would need next. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Decorative slides with no sources fail the history purpose. Correct the claim or use of sources, not just the neatness of the poster.
